entities.summary:
Bernardo Bandini Baroncelli was a Florentine merchant and a key figure in the Pazzi conspiracy, a plot to remove the Medici family from power in Florence in 1478. He was born into a prominent family and married into another influential clan, forging alliances that would fuel the conspiracy.

The Pazzi family, who sought to overthrow the Medici, had been a thorn in the side of the powerful banking family for years. The plot was masterminded by Jacopo de' Pazzi, a cousin of the Pope, and his co-conspirators, who hoped to install a new ruler in Florence and gain control of the city's lucrative trade and commerce. However, the plot was ultimately foiled when Bandini's own family refused to support him, and he was arrested and executed on December 29, 1479.

 The aftermath of the failed Pazzi conspiracy had far-reaching consequences for Florence and the wider Italian peninsula. The Medici family, having narrowly escaped overthrow, tightened their grip on power, and the city's politics became even more faction-ridden. The event also marked a turning point in the struggle between the powerful city-states of Italy, as the Medici's influence extended across the region.

 The Pazzi conspiracy, in which Bandini played a pivotal role, continues to fascinate historians and scholars today. It represents a pivotal moment in the complex web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that defined the politics of Renaissance Italy.

 Bandini's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his actions and decisions had a lasting impact on the course of Florentine history. The Pazzi conspiracy, in which he was a key player, remains a fascinating example of the intrigue and deception that characterized the politics of the Renaissance.
